newsitem.title: UK: Gold Council helps UK M and S stores on jewellery.
newsitem.headline: Gold Council helps UK M and S stores on jewellery.

text.p: The World Gold Council (WGC) supplied market analysis and training for staff in the lead up to a move by UK store group Marks and Spencer Plc into retailing gold jewellery, the WGC said on Wednesday.
The UK retailer of food, clothing and homeware launched its jewellery line in nine stores in September this year and said on Wednesday it had since increased the number of outlets to 11.
WGC UK manager for jewellery Jan Springer said WGC research showed that 60 percent of jewellery was bought in the UK by women either for themselves or for other women.
There were 24 million women in the country of whom 43 percent were workers and Springer said it was an advantage to busy shoppers to have jewellery and clothing in one store.
The Marks and Spencers' range of earrings, neck and wrist wear would be in nine and 18 carat gold, she said.
Springer said Marks and Spencers planned to include its jewellery outlets in around 40 stores by third quarter 1997.
The WGC is a promotional and statistical group backed by a number of gold producers. It monitors and promotes uses for gold in countries accounting for about 75 percent of world demand.
